result: This manuscript describes a Registered Report for the Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology, which aims to replicate key experiments from Lu et al. (2012) published in Nature. The original paper was selected based on citations and Altmetric scores from papers published between 2010 and 2012.
evaluation: Claims C1-C4 describe the project context and paper selection methodology, all supported by appropriate citations (Errington et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2012). These are factual statements about the replication project design and are well-documented.

result: IDH1 and IDH2 mutations are associated with multiple cancer types including gliomas, acute myeloid leukemias, chondrosarcomas, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas, lymphomas, melanomas, and colon, thyroid, and prostate cancers.
evaluation: Claims C9-C17 summarize established knowledge about IDH mutation associations with various cancers, all supported by citation to a review (Krell et al., 2013). This represents well-established prior work in the field.

result: IDH mutations alter enzyme specificity such that mutant IDH proteins produce 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG) instead of α-ketoglutarate from isocitrate, and 2HG is an oncometabolite with oncogenic effects.
evaluation: Claims C18-C19 describe the established biochemical mechanism of IDH mutations, supported by multiple citations (Krell et al., 2013; McKenney and Levine, 2013; Ward et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2013). This represents well-established prior knowledge.

result: Lu et al. (2012) demonstrated that expression of mutant IDH1 or IDH2 in 293T cells caused global increases in histone methylation markers and increased intracellular 2HG levels, as assessed by Western blot and metabolite analysis.
evaluation: Claims C5-C6 and C26-C28 describe findings from the original Lu et al. (2012) study, specifically Figure 1B. These are appropriately cited and represent the key findings being targeted for replication in Protocol 1.

result: Lu et al. (2012) showed that 2HG interferes with global demethylation required for differentiation. In 3T3-L1 cells, mutant IDH expression increased methylation and blocked adipocyte differentiation as measured by Oil-Red-O staining and adipocyte marker expression.
evaluation: Claims C20-C22 and C29-C32 describe the differentiation block phenotype from Lu et al. (2012), Figures 2A, 2B, and 2D. These findings are appropriately cited and represent key results being replicated in Protocol 2.

result: Lu et al. (2012) demonstrated that the differentiation block is mediated by the 2HG-sensitive histone demethylase KDM4C, as knockdown of KDM4C recapitulated the phenotype of 2HG production by increasing methylation and inhibiting differentiation.
evaluation: Claims C7-C8 and C23-C24, C33-C35 describe the mechanistic role of KDM4C from Lu et al. (2012), Figure 4D. These findings are appropriately cited and represent the key mechanistic result being replicated in Protocol 3.

result: Lu et al. (2012) found a correlation between IDH mutation status and overall methylation levels in glioma samples.
evaluation: Claim C25 describes a clinical correlation from the original study, appropriately cited to Lu et al. (2012). This extends the in vitro findings to patient samples.

result: Multiple independent studies have corroborated that mutant IDH expression increases methylation levels in various cell types and model systems, including human tumor cell lines, mouse models, and patient samples.
evaluation: Claims C36-C43 describe corroborating evidence from multiple independent studies (Duncan et al., 2012; Kernytsky et al., 2015; Turcan et al., 2012; Londono Gentile et al., 2013; Ward et al., 2013; Sasaki et al., 2012; Akbay et al., 2014; Venneti et al., 2013). All claims are appropriately cited and demonstrate reproducibility of the core findings across different systems.

result: The replication study will maintain 293T and 3T3-L1 cells in DMEM with 10% FBS at 37°C/5% CO2, with STR profiling and mycoplasma testing.
evaluation: Claims C44-C45 describe standard cell culture conditions and quality control measures for the replication study. These are appropriate methodological details.

result: All experimental data from the replication study will be made publicly available through publication or the Open Science Framework.
evaluation: Claim C46 describes the data sharing plan for the replication study. This is a clear commitment to open science practices.
